title: Quality of Life of Couples Dealing with Cancer: Dyadic and Individual Adjustment among Breast and Prostate Cancer Survivors and Their Spousal Caregivers

sentence: Reviews of determinants of quality of life in children with cancer and survivors indicate that outcomes are shaped by interacting medical, psychosocial, and contextual factors, yet parental studies have often relied on narrow outcome sets and insufficient stratification by family, treatment, and survivorship characteristics ref [16].
title: Disability, psychological distress and quality of life in breast cancer survivors with arm lymphedema.

sentence: Evidence from a racially diverse cohort of breast cancer survivors demonstrates that posttraumatic growth and health-related quality of life can be meaningfully examined together and that culturally diverse samples can reveal patterns obscured in homogeneous cohorts ref [18].
title: Social networks and health-related quality of life in breast cancer survivors: a prospective study.

sentence: Work on the PedsQL demonstrates the value of standardized quality-of-life measurement in childhood cancer survivorship and suggests a useful template for linking survivor functioning to family outcomes, yet parental studies have not consistently integrated such multidimensional instruments into longitudinal designs ref [14].
title: Long‐term follow‐up of pediatric cancer survivors: Education, surveillance, and screening

sentence: Long-term survivors of childhood central nervous system malignancies often experience substantial neurocognitive, physical, and functional sequelae, implying a potentially prolonged and distinctive burden on parents that remains insufficiently characterized in psychosocial studies ref [11].
title: Long-term survivors of childhood central nervous system malignancies: the experience of the Childhood Cancer Survivor Study.

sentence: Similarly, risk-stratification work from the Childhood Cancer Survivor Study underscores that some survivor subgroups carry elevated long-term morbidity and therefore may require more intensive surveillance and support, but parent-focused research has rarely used these risk-based frameworks to guide sampling, subgroup analysis, or intervention targeting ref [11].
title: Long-term survivors of childhood central nervous system malignancies: the experience of the Childhood Cancer Survivor Study.

sentence: Accordingly, future research should align parental psychosocial inquiry with survivorship care models that emphasize education, surveillance, and screening across the life course ref [15].
